title: Founding Pershing Square with a concentrated activist model
statement: After winding up Gotham Partners, Ackman launched Pershing Square to hold large, public, research-intensive positions in a handful of companies and push for changes to unlock value.
outcome: The fund produced some of the industry's best early years, including returns above 40% in 2009, and became the most prominent activist platform of its generation.

title: MBIA short — the five-year bet against the bond insurer
statement: Ackman analyzed MBIA's structured-finance guarantees and concluded the company was insolvent on any realistic reading of its exposures; he shorted the stock and published his research publicly.
outcome: Vilified and investigated for years, he was vindicated when the 2008 crisis broke the monolines; the research became legendary for its rigor, though the profits were modest relative to the effort.

title: General Growth Properties — buying the bankrupt mall REIT
statement: When the second-largest mall operator filed for bankruptcy in the crisis, Ackman determined the assets were worth multiples of the distressed equity price and bought roughly 25% of the shares at the bottom.
outcome: The equity emerged from bankruptcy and rose dramatically; Pershing's roughly $60 million position turned into over $1 billion — the firm's signature crisis win.

title: J.C. Penney — the failed turnaround bet
statement: Ackman bought about a quarter of the retailer and hired Ron Johnson from Apple to eliminate discounts and transform stores into a collection of branded boutiques.
outcome: The strategy catastrophically alienated the customer base: sales fell roughly 25% in a year, Johnson was fired, and Pershing exited at a loss approaching $500 million. It remains Ackman's most-cited operational overreach.

title: Herbalife — the billion-dollar short of the nutrition company
statement: Ackman publicly shorted roughly $1 billion of Herbalife, calling it a pyramid scheme destined for regulatory shutdown, in the most publicized activist short of the era.
outcome: The stock roughly tripled from his average short price amid a squeeze; Carl Icahn took the opposite side. Ackman covered in 2018 at a loss of about $1 billion — the lesson he drew publicly was that his thesis might have been right but the bet structure was unbounded.

title: Canadian Pacific — the activist railway turnaround
statement: Ackman won a proxy fight at CP, replaced the CEO with Hunter Harrison, and forced the operating-ratio transformation of a railroad long considered unfixable.
outcome: The operating ratio fell from the mid-80s toward 60; the stock roughly quintupled, and the campaign became the textbook case of operational activism.

title: COVID crash — buying Hilton, Lowe's and restaurant stocks at the bottom
statement: With markets in free fall, Ackman went on CNBC in an emotional segment and bought beaten-down hospitality and retail equities with a large portion of Pershing's capital.
outcome: The March 2020 bottom purchases produced a 70% gain for the year 2020, Pershing's best ever.

title: Universal Music spinout — the largest holding restructure
statement: Ackman accumulated roughly 10% of Universal Music and drove its distribution from Vivendi, later distributing the stake to shareholders after an abandoned SPAC structure.
outcome: The position became Pershing's largest holding at a valuation in the tens of billions; the episode demonstrated his willingness to hold 'franchise' assets semi-permanently.
